rows.reasoning: 7C3=35; 3Π4=3^4=81; 3H4=C(6,4)=15, so all three statements are true.
The opened 6-by-4 grid places R four steps right and three up from P, then two right and one up to Q. Count C(7,4)×C(3,1)=35×3=105.
The multinomial term count is C(8,2)×7=28×7=196. Positive solutions a+b+c=7 are C(6,2)=15. Sum=211.
There are 2^k strings of length k. Lengths 1 through n total 2^(n+1)−2; n=7 gives 254 and n=8 gives 510, so minimum n=8.
The x^3 and x^2 coefficients are 80a^2 and −40a^3. Their sum is 40a^2(2−a)=0; positive a=2.
In (x+1/x)^5, coefficients of x^3 and x^1 are 5 and 10. The x^3 coefficient after multiplication is 10−2×5=0.
Use r C(n,r)=n C(n−1,r−1) for the first blanks and C(n,r)=C(n,n−r) for the symmetry blank; this is choice ⑤.
The binomial sum is 2^n−1. 2000<2^n−1<3000 gives n=11; 2^n−1=255 gives n=8. Sum=19.
Treat the grandparents as one block: 5 objects around a circle give 4! arrangements, with 2 orders inside the block, totaling 48? Wait circular objects count is (5−1)!×2=48. Select choice ③.
Choose the omitted color in 7 ways. Six distinct colors on six cyclic sectors modulo the six rotations give 6!/6=120. Total 840.
The regular hexagonal table has rotational symmetry of order 6. The 12 distinct people have 12!/6=2×11! arrangements modulo rotation.
There are 5^3 functions and 5P3=60 injections, so the probability is 60/125=12/25.
Favorable selections are C(5,2)C(3,1)=30; all selections are C(8,3)=56. Probability=15/28.
Put t=b+1 (2≤t≤6). For each t, a has t choices and c≤d≤e in [t,6] has C(9−t,3) choices. Sum 2·35+3·20+4·10+5·4+6·1=196.
All nonnegative triples summing to 12: C(14,2)=91. For each coordinate equal to 2, 11 triples; subtract 3·11 and add back the 3 pairwise intersections: 91−33+3=61.

There are C(11,5)=462 nondecreasing six-term sequences from 1..6. Count sequences with f2,f5 both not divisible by 3 by summing b∈{1,2,4,5}, e∈{b,4,5} (e from {1,2,4,5}): b·C(e−b+2,2)·(7−e)=213. Valid=462−213=249.
The number of 3-element subsets of {1,...,10} with no consecutive entries is C(10−3+1,3)=56. Assigning the 3 distinct students gives 56×3!=336.
A nonnegative distributions count is C(14,4)=1001. Positive distributions count is C(9,4)=126. A+B=1127.
Real roots require discriminant 4a^2−12b≥0, i.e. a^2≥3b. For a=1..6 the eligible b counts are 0,1,3,5,6,6, totaling 21 of 36 outcomes, hence 7/12.
Each of 10 elements independently lies outside S3, in S3 only, in S2 and S3, or in all three, giving 4^10=1,048,576 strict chains.
